source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a new speech, given in the plains of Moab before Israel crosses the Jordan
decisions.reason: Israel is still camped in the plains of Moab across from Jericho (33:48-50; 36:13). The last speech ended with the command to drive out the people of Canaan and divide the land by lot (33:50-56). This one sets out the borders of that land (verses 1-15) and names the men who will divide it (verses 16-29).

source.text: צַ֞ו אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֲלֵהֶ֔ם כִּֽי־אַתֶּ֥ם בָּאִ֖ים אֶל־הָאָ֣רֶץ כְּנָ֑עַן זֹ֣את הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּפֹּ֤ל לָכֶם֙ בְּֽנַחֲלָ֔ה אֶ֥רֶץ כְּנַ֖עַן לִגְבֻלֹתֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Command [the] sons of Israel and say to them, When you [are] coming into the land [of] Canaan, this [is] the land that will fall to you as an inheritance, [the] land of Canaan by its borders,

en.L: "Command the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel and say to them, 'When you come into the land of Canaan, this [is] the land that will fall to you as an inheritance, the land of Canaan by its borders:
en.B: "Give the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this command and tell them: 'You are about to enter the land of Canaan. Here is the land that will fall to you as your inheritance, the land of Canaan with these borders:
en.R: "Give the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} these orders. Tell them, 'Soon you will go into the land of Canaan. This is the land that will be given to you by lot to be your own. Here are its borders.

decisions.choice: you are coming: you are about to enter
decisions.reason: The verb form describes something happening now or about to happen. Israel has not yet crossed the Jordan; the borders are given ahead of time, as the laws of 33:51 and 35:10 are.

decisions.choice: will fall to you: will come to you by lot
decisions.reason: Land is said to "fall" to someone because it was shared out by casting lots (verse 13; 26:55-56; Joshua 17:5). The land is not taken by Israel's own choice; it is given to them.

decisions.choice: inheritance: a share of land held for good and handed down in the family
decisions.reason: The word means a possession that belongs to a family or tribe and passes from parents to children. The land is Israel's inheritance because the LORD gives it to them, as he promised their ancestors (Genesis 15:18; Exodus 6:8).

decisions.choice: will be given to you by lot to be your own
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of land "falling" to someone (m2) and what an inheritance is (m3).

source.text: וְהָיָ֨ה לָכֶ֧ם פְּאַת־נֶ֛גֶב מִמִּדְבַּר־צִ֖ן עַל־יְדֵ֣י אֱד֑וֹם וְהָיָ֤ה לָכֶם֙ גְּב֣וּל נֶ֔גֶב מִקְצֵ֥ה יָם־הַמֶּ֖לַח קֵֽדְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will be for you [the] side [of the] south from [the] wilderness of Zin along [the] hands of Edom, and will be for you [the] border [of the] south from [the] end of [the] Sea of the Salt eastward,

en.L: your south side will be from the wilderness of Zin along the side of Edom, and your south border will be from the end of the Salt Sea on the east.
en.B: Your southern side will take in the wilderness of Zin, alongside Edom. On the east, your southern border will start at the end of the Dead Sea.
en.R: In the south, your land will include the Zin Desert, next to the land of Edom. The southern border will begin in the east, at the southern tip of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: the four borders, given in order: south, west, north, east
decisions.reason: The chapter traces the land's edges one side at a time: south (verses 3-5), west (verse 6), north (verses 7-9) and east (verses 10-12). The same southern line marks the edge of Judah in Joshua 15:1-4, and Ezekiel's picture of the land in the age to come uses much of the northern and eastern line (Ezekiel 47:15-20). The land described is Canaan west of the Jordan; it does not include the land east of the river (verses 14-15).

decisions.choice: along the hands of Edom: alongside Edom's territory
decisions.reason: "Hands" here means sides or edges, as in a place lying "at the hand of" another. The wilderness of Zin runs beside the land of Edom, which lay to the south-east (20:16, 23).

decisions.choice: the Salt Sea: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The Salt Sea is the Dead Sea, as in Genesis 14:3. The border starts at its southern end and runs west.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea; the Zin Desert (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the modern name for the Salt Sea, as in Genesis 14:3; Literal keeps "Salt Sea". Readable calls the wilderness of Zin "the Zin Desert", as in 13:21.

decisions.choice: the southern tip
decisions.reason: The end of the sea from which a southern border runs west must be its southern end. Readable says so; Literal and Balanced keep "the end".

source.text: וְנָסַ֣ב לָכֶם֩ הַגְּב֨וּל מִנֶּ֜גֶב לְמַעֲלֵ֤ה עַקְרַבִּים֙ וְעָ֣בַר צִ֔נָה וְהָיוּ֙ תּֽוֹצְאֹתָ֔יו מִנֶּ֖גֶב לְקָדֵ֣שׁ בַּרְנֵ֑עַ וְיָצָ֥א חֲצַר־אַדָּ֖ר וְעָבַ֥ר עַצְמֹֽנָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will turn for you the border from [the] south to [the] ascent of Akrabbim, and will pass on to Zin, and will be its goings out from [the] south to Kadesh-barnea, and will go out [to] Hazar-addar, and will pass on to Azmon,

en.L: And the border will turn for you south of the ascent of Akrabbim and pass on to Zin, and its end will be south of Kadesh-barnea; and it will go out to Hazar-addar and pass on to Azmon.
en.B: From there your border will turn and run south of the Ascent of Akrabbim and on to Zin, reaching as far as the south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go out to Hazar-addar and on to Azmon.
en.R: From there it will turn and pass south of Scorpion Pass and go on through Zin. Its farthest point will be south of Kadesh-barnea. Then it will go on to Hazar-addar and over to Azmon.

decisions.choice: the ascent of Akrabbim: the Scorpions' Pass
decisions.reason: Akrabbim means "scorpions", and the "ascent" is a road climbing up a steep slope. It was a pass going up from the desert south-west of the Dead Sea into the hills (Joshua 15:3; Judges 1:36).

decisions.choice: its goings out: the point the border reaches
decisions.reason: The plural word means the places where something goes out to, its farthest reach or end. It is used of each border in this chapter (verses 5, 8, 9, 12). Here, in the middle of the line, it marks how far south the border dips, below Kadesh-barnea.

decisions.choice: they will be: the reading the scribes marked
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text (ketiv) read "it will be"; the reading the scribes marked (qere), followed here, is "they will be", agreeing with the plural "its goings out". The meaning is the same either way.

decisions.choice: Kadesh-barnea, Hazar-addar, Azmon: places on the southern edge
decisions.reason: Kadesh-barnea is the oasis where Israel camped for a long time and from which the scouts were sent (13:26; 20:1; 32:8). Hazar-addar and Azmon lay between Kadesh and the Wadi of Egypt; where exactly is not known. Joshua 15:3-4 traces the same line, with Hezron and Addar for Hazar-addar.

decisions.choice: the Ascent of Akrabbim (B); Scorpion Pass (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the place name as a name; Readable says what it means (m1).

source.text: וְנָסַ֧ב הַגְּב֛וּל מֵעַצְמ֖וֹן נַ֣חְלָה מִצְרָ֑יִם וְהָי֥וּ תוֹצְאֹתָ֖יו הַיָּֽמָּה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will turn the border from Azmon [to the] wadi of Egypt, and will be its goings out at the sea.

en.L: And the border will turn from Azmon to the brook of Egypt, and its end will be at the sea.
en.B: From Azmon the border will bend around to the Wadi of Egypt and end at the sea.
en.R: At Azmon it will turn toward the Wadi of Egypt, a stream that is dry most of the year. It will end at the Mediterranean Sea.

decisions.choice: the wadi of Egypt: the stream bed between Canaan and Egypt
decisions.reason: The word means a valley with a stream that flows only in the rainy season. The Wadi of Egypt marked the edge of Canaan toward Egypt, in the desert of northern Sinai (Joshua 15:4, 47; 1 Kings 8:65; Isaiah 27:12). It is not the Nile, which is called by a different word.

decisions.choice: the sea: the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The southern border runs west to the coast of the Great Sea, which forms the western border (verse 6).

decisions.choice: brook (L), Wadi (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses the common English word "brook". Balanced and Readable use "wadi", the word for a dry stream bed in this part of the world, as the name of the place; Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable names the sea (m2).

source.text: וּגְב֣וּל יָ֔ם וְהָיָ֥ה לָכֶ֛ם הַיָּ֥ם הַגָּד֖וֹל וּגְב֑וּל זֶֽה־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֥וּל יָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] border [of the] west: and will be for you the Sea the Great and [its] border; this will be for you [the] border [of the] west.

en.L: And [as for] the western border, the Great Sea and [its] coast will be [the border] for you; this will be your western border.
en.B: Your western border will be the Great Sea and its coast. That will be your border on the west.
en.R: In the west, the border will be the coast of the Mediterranean Sea. That will be your western border.

decisions.choice: the Great Sea: the Mediterranean
decisions.reason: The Great Sea is the Mediterranean, the sea along the whole western side of Canaan (Joshua 1:4; 15:12).

decisions.choice: west: literally "sea"
decisions.reason: The word for "west" is the word "sea", because the sea lay to the west of the land. Here the same word stands for both, with the sea itself as the western border.

decisions.choice: and its border: the coast
decisions.reason: The word "border" here means the edge of the sea, its coastline, which is the land's boundary on that side. Joshua 15:12 uses the same words for Judah's western border.

decisions.choice: [as for] ... [its] ... [the border]
decisions.reason: The Hebrew states the heading first, "the western border", then what it is. Literal supplies words so the clause can be read in English.

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: Readable uses the modern name of the Great Sea (m1).

source.text: וְזֶֽה־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֣וּל צָפ֑וֹן מִן־הַיָּם֙ הַגָּדֹ֔ל תְּתָא֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם הֹ֥ר הָהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And this will be for you [the] border [of the] north: from the Sea the Great you will mark out for yourselves Hor the mountain.

en.L: And this will be your northern border: from the Great Sea you will mark out for yourselves [a line to] Mount Hor.
en.B: This will be your northern border: from the Great Sea mark out a line to Mount Hor.
en.R: In the north, draw your border line from the Mediterranean Sea to Mount Hor.

decisions.choice: you will mark out: draw a line
decisions.reason: The verb is rare; here and in verse 8 it means to mark out a boundary or draw a line from one point to the next. Verse 10 uses a similar verb in the same sense.

decisions.choice: Mount Hor: a mountain in the north, not the place where Aaron died
alternatives: the same Mount Hor as in 20:22
decisions.reason: This Mount Hor has the same name as the mountain on the edge of Edom where Aaron died (20:22-29; 33:37-39), but it lies on the northern border, somewhere between the coast and Lebo-hamath, perhaps in the mountains of Lebanon. Which peak it was is not known.

decisions.choice: [a line to] (L), a line to (B), draw your border line (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "you will mark out Mount Hor". English needs "a line to" to make sense of it; Literal brackets it.

decisions.choice: the Mediterranean Sea
decisions.reason: As in verse 6.

source.text: מֵהֹ֣ר הָהָ֔ר תְּתָא֖וּ לְבֹ֣א חֲמָ֑ת וְהָי֛וּ תּוֹצְאֹ֥ת הַגְּבֻ֖ל צְדָֽדָה׃

records.literal_gloss: From Hor the mountain you will mark out [to] Lebo-hamath, and will be [the] goings out of the border at Zedad.

en.L: From Mount Hor you will mark out [a line to] Lebo-hamath, and the end of the border will be at Zedad.
en.B: From Mount Hor mark it out to Lebo-hamath, and the border will reach out to Zedad.
en.R: From Mount Hor, draw it to Lebo-hamath and on to Zedad.

decisions.choice: Lebo-hamath: a place name, or "the entrance of Hamath"
decisions.reason: As at 13:21, the words can be the name of a town or "the way into Hamath", the pass leading north into the land of Hamath in Syria. Either way it marks the northern edge of the land (1 Kings 8:65; Ezekiel 47:20).

decisions.choice: Zedad: a town on the far north-eastern border
decisions.reason: Zedad is named again on the northern border in Ezekiel 47:15. Its site is not known for certain.

decisions.choice: [a line to] (L), mark it out to (B)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

source.text: וְיָצָ֤א הַגְּבֻל֙ זִפְרֹ֔נָה וְהָי֥וּ תוֹצְאֹתָ֖יו חֲצַ֣ר עֵינָ֑ן זֶֽה־יִהְיֶ֥ה לָכֶ֖ם גְּב֥וּל צָפֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go out the border to Ziphron, and will be its goings out [at] Hazar-enan; this will be for you [the] border [of the] north.

en.L: And the border will go out to Ziphron, and its end will be at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern border.
en.B: The border will continue to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. This will be your northern border.
en.R: Then it will go on to Ziphron and end at Hazar-enan. That will be your border in the north.

decisions.choice: Ziphron, Hazar-enan: the north-eastern end of the border
decisions.reason: Hazar-enan probably means "village of springs". It marks the corner where the northern border meets the eastern one (verse 10), as in Ezekiel 47:17 and 48:1. Ziphron is not named anywhere else, and neither site is known for certain.

source.text: וְהִתְאַוִּיתֶ֥ם לָכֶ֖ם לִגְב֣וּל קֵ֑דְמָה מֵחֲצַ֥ר עֵינָ֖ן שְׁפָֽמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And you will mark out for yourselves for [the] border eastward from Hazar-enan to Shepham,

en.L: And you will mark out for yourselves [a line] for the eastern border from Hazar-enan to Shepham,
en.B: For your eastern border, mark out a line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.
en.R: In the east, draw your border line from Hazar-enan to Shepham.

decisions.choice: you will mark out: draw a line
decisions.reason: The verb here is spelled like a verb that means "to desire", but that sense does not fit. It is a form with the same meaning as the verb in verses 7-8, to mark out a boundary, either a variant of that verb or a closely related one.

decisions.choice: [a line] (L), a line (B), draw your border line (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 7.

source.text: וְיָרַ֨ד הַגְּבֻ֧ל מִשְּׁפָ֛ם הָרִבְלָ֖ה מִקֶּ֣דֶם לָעָ֑יִן וְיָרַ֣ד הַגְּב֔וּל וּמָחָ֛ה עַל־כֶּ֥תֶף יָם־כִּנֶּ֖רֶת קֵֽדְמָה׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go down the border from Shepham [to] the Riblah, on [the] east of the Ain, and will go down the border and will strike against [the] shoulder of [the] Sea of Chinnereth eastward,

en.L: and the border will go down from Shepham to Riblah, on the east side of Ain; and the border will go down and strike against the slope of the Sea of Chinnereth on the east.
en.B: From Shepham the border will go down to Riblah, on the east side of Ain, and on down until it meets the slopes east of the Sea of Chinnereth.
en.R: From Shepham it will go down to Riblah, on the east side of Ain. Then it will go on down to the hills along the east shore of the Sea of Chinnereth (Lake Galilee).

decisions.choice: Riblah and Ain: places on the eastern border
alternatives: Riblah in the land of Hamath
decisions.reason: Both names have "the" in front of them, "the Riblah" and "the Ain", and Ain means "spring". It is not certain whether this Riblah is the town in the land of Hamath where kings of Babylon and Egypt later held court (2 Kings 23:33; 25:6), which lies far to the north, or another place nearer the lake. The site of Ain is not known.

decisions.choice: strike against the shoulder: reach the slope
decisions.reason: "Shoulder" is used for the side of a hill or a ridge. The border runs down until it touches the high ground that rises from the east side of the lake.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Chinnereth: the lake later called the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Chinnereth was a town on the western shore (Joshua 19:35), and the lake took its name (Joshua 12:3; 13:27). In the Gospels it is the Sea of Galilee or the Lake of Gennesaret (Luke 5:1).

decisions.choice: (Lake Galilee)
decisions.reason: Readable adds the lake's later name, which most readers know.

decisions.choice: Riblah, Ain, without "the"
decisions.reason: English does not put "the" before a town's name, so the article is left out at every level; m1 notes it.

source.text: וְיָרַ֤ד הַגְּבוּל֙ הַיַּרְדֵּ֔נָה וְהָי֥וּ תוֹצְאֹתָ֖יו יָ֣ם הַמֶּ֑לַח זֹאת֩ תִּהְיֶ֨ה לָכֶ֥ם הָאָ֛רֶץ לִגְבֻלֹתֶ֖יהָ סָבִֽיב׃

records.literal_gloss: And will go down the border to the Jordan, and will be its goings out [at the] Sea of the Salt. This will be for you the land by its borders all around.

en.L: And the border will go down to the Jordan, and its end will be at the Salt Sea. This will be your land, by its borders all around.'"
en.B: Then the border will go down along the Jordan and end at the Dead Sea. This will be your land, with its borders on every side.'"
en.R: Then it will follow the Jordan River down to the Dead Sea. Those are the borders of your land on every side.'"

decisions.choice: the Jordan: the eastern border
decisions.reason: From the Sea of Chinnereth the border follows the Jordan down to the Dead Sea, where the southern border began (verse 3), and so the line closes. The land east of the Jordan, already given to two and a half tribes (32:33; verses 14-15), lies outside the land of Canaan described here; this is why the eastern tribes had to show they belonged to Israel (Joshua 22:24-27).

decisions.choice: this will be your land: the summary that closes the description
decisions.reason: The words answer verse 2: "this is the land ... the land of Canaan by its borders". All that lies between the four lines is the land given to Israel.

decisions.choice: the Dead Sea; the Jordan River (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3. Readable calls the Jordan a river.

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו מֹשֶׁ֔ה אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר זֹ֣את הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּתְנַחֲל֤וּ אֹתָהּ֙ בְּגוֹרָ֔ל אֲשֶׁר֙ צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֔ה לָתֵ֛ת לְתִשְׁעַ֥ת הַמַּטּ֖וֹת וַחֲצִ֥י הַמַּטֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And commanded Moses [the] sons of Israel, saying, This [is] the land that you will receive as inheritance by lot, which commanded Yahweh to give to [the] nine tribes and [the] half of the tribe.

en.L: And Moses commanded the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, saying, "This [is] the land which you will receive as an inheritance by lot, which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded to give to the nine tribes and the half of the tribe.
en.B: Moses gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} this command: "This is the land you are to divide among yourselves by lot as your inheritance. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded that it be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe.
en.R: Moses told the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, "This is the land you will receive as your own. You will divide it by drawing lots. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has commanded that it be given to the nine tribes and to half of the tribe of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: by lot: the shares decided by casting lots
decisions.reason: The land was to be shared out by lot (26:55-56; 33:54), so that the choice of which tribe received which region was left to the LORD, not to the leaders (Proverbs 16:33). Joshua 14:2 and 18:10 tell how it was done.

decisions.choice: you will receive as an inheritance: take as your own possession, each tribe its share
decisions.reason: The verb form means to receive something as one's inheritance, here with the sense of taking possession of it among themselves, tribe by tribe. The same form is used in 32:18 and 33:54.

decisions.choice: the nine tribes and the half of the tribe: the tribes that settle west of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Twelve tribes share the land, with Joseph counted as two (Ephraim and Manasseh) and Levi given no tribal land (18:20-24; 35:1-8). Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh settle east of the Jordan (chapter 32; verses 14-15), so nine and a half tribes remain for Canaan. The half-tribe is the other half of Manasseh (Joshua 14:1-3; 17:1-6).

decisions.choice: half of the tribe of Manasseh
decisions.reason: Readable names the tribe, as verse 14 does (m3).

source.text: כִּ֣י לָקְח֞וּ מַטֵּ֨ה בְנֵ֤י הָראוּבֵנִי֙ לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֔ם וּמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־הַגָּדִ֖י לְבֵ֣ית אֲבֹתָ֑ם וַחֲצִי֙ מַטֵּ֣ה מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לָקְח֖וּ נַחֲלָתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: For have taken [the] tribe of [the] sons of the Reubenite[s] by [the] house of their fathers, and [the] tribe of [the] sons of the Gadite[s] by [the] house of their fathers, and [the] half of [the] tribe of Manasseh, have taken their inheritance.

en.L: For the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of the Reubenites by the house of their fathers, and the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of the Gadites by the house of their fathers, have received [theirs], and the half of the tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance.
en.B: For the tribe of the Reubenites and the tribe of the Gadites, by their ancestral families, have already received their inheritance, and so has the half-tribe of Manasseh.
en.R: The tribe of Reuben and the tribe of Gad, family by family, have already received their land, and so has half of the tribe of Manasseh.

decisions.choice: for: the reason the land is shared by only nine and a half tribes
alternatives: a note by the narrator outside the speech
decisions.reason: Verses 14-15 explain verse 13. They may be the end of Moses' words to the people or a note added by the narrator; either way they give the reason, and the sense does not change.

decisions.choice: have taken: their share is already settled
decisions.reason: The verb "have taken" is said twice, once at the start and once at the end of the long subject. The two and a half tribes have already been given their land east of the Jordan by Moses (32:33), even though their men must still cross and fight with the rest (32:20-22, 29).

decisions.choice: by the house of their fathers: family by family
decisions.reason: The "house of the fathers" is the extended family traced through the male line, a unit within the clan (1:2). Even the eastern land was given out family by family.

decisions.choice: [theirs]
decisions.reason: The first "have taken" has no object in Hebrew until the end of the verse; Literal brackets "theirs" so it can stand where it is.

decisions.choice: one verb, "have already received"
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "have received" once and add "already", which gives the force of the past tense (m2).

source.text: שְׁנֵ֥י הַמַּטּ֖וֹת וַחֲצִ֣י הַמַּטֶּ֑ה לָקְח֣וּ נַחֲלָתָ֗ם מֵעֵ֛בֶר לְיַרְדֵּ֥ן יְרֵח֖וֹ קֵ֥דְמָה מִזְרָֽחָה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: [The] two tribes and [the] half of the tribe have taken their inheritance from [the] other side of [the] Jordan [at] Jericho, eastward, toward [the] sunrise.

en.L: The two tribes and the half of the tribe have received their inheritance across the Jordan [from] Jericho, eastward, toward the sunrise."
en.B: These two tribes and the half-tribe have received their inheritance across the Jordan from Jericho, on the east, toward the sunrise."
en.R: These two and a half tribes have received their land on the east side of the Jordan River, across from Jericho, where the sun rises."

decisions.choice: across the Jordan from Jericho: on the east bank, facing Jericho
decisions.reason: As in 22:1, "beyond the Jordan" is said from the side of the land west of the river. Here the phrase is made clear by "eastward, toward the sunrise".

decisions.choice: eastward, toward the sunrise: two words for east
decisions.reason: The first word means "in front", since east was the direction one faced; the second means "the rising" of the sun. Together they stress that this land lies to the east.

decisions.choice: two and a half tribes
decisions.reason: Readable puts "the two tribes and the half of the tribe" as a single number.

source.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses. He said,
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

decisions.choice: a second speech: the men who will divide the land
decisions.reason: The words of verse 1 open a new section. The LORD has set the borders (verses 1-12); now he names who is to share out the land inside them.

source.text: אֵ֚לֶּה שְׁמ֣וֹת הָֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־יִנְחֲל֥וּ לָכֶ֖ם אֶת־הָאָ֑רֶץ אֶלְעָזָר֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וִיהוֹשֻׁ֖עַ בִּן־נֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are the] names of the men who will apportion for you the land: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.

en.L: "These [are] the names of the men who will give you the land as an inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
en.B: "These are the names of the men who are to divide the land among you as your inheritance: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
en.R: "Here are the names of the men who will divide up the land and give each of you your share: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.

decisions.choice: apportion for you: give you the land as an inheritance, sharing it out
decisions.reason: The verb is the one from which "inheritance" comes. With "for you" it means to put the people in possession of the land by dividing it among them. The same task is given to the tribal leaders in verse 18 and summed up in verse 29.

decisions.choice: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun: the leaders after Moses
decisions.reason: Eleazar took Aaron's place as high priest (20:25-28), and Joshua was appointed to lead the people after Moses, standing before Eleazar (27:18-23). Moses will not enter the land (27:12-14), so these two will divide it, as Joshua 14:1 and 19:51 record.

decisions.choice: for you: the people as a whole
decisions.reason: "You" is plural. The LORD speaks to Moses, but the land is divided for all Israel.

decisions.choice: divide up the land and give each of you your share
decisions.reason: Readable spells out both parts of the verb: dividing the land and giving it to the people (m1).

source.text: וְנָשִׂ֥יא אֶחָ֛ד נָשִׂ֥יא אֶחָ֖ד מִמַּטֶּ֑ה תִּקְח֖וּ לִנְחֹ֥ל אֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And one leader, one leader from [a] tribe, you will take to apportion the land.

en.L: And one leader, one leader from [each] tribe, you will take to give out the land as an inheritance.
en.B: You are also to take one leader from every tribe to divide up the land.
en.R: Also choose one leader from each tribe to help divide up the land.

decisions.choice: one leader, one leader: one from each tribe
decisions.reason: Saying "one leader" twice means one for every tribe, the same pattern used for the scouts in 13:2.

decisions.choice: a leader from each tribe: men of the new generation
decisions.reason: The ten tribes that settle west of the Jordan each send a leader (verses 19-28); Reuben and Gad have their land already, and Levi receives no tribal land. None of these men except Caleb appears among the leaders or scouts of the earlier lists (1:5-15; 13:4-15). The old generation had died in the wilderness (26:64-65).

decisions.choice: you will take: plural, Moses and the people
decisions.reason: The verb is plural, as "for you" is in verse 17.

decisions.choice: [each]
decisions.reason: Literal brackets "each", which English needs to make sense of "from tribe".

decisions.choice: to help
decisions.reason: The leaders work with Eleazar and Joshua, as Joshua 14:1 shows. Readable adds "help" to show they share the task with the two men named in verse 17.

source.text: וְאֵ֖לֶּה שְׁמ֣וֹת הָאֲנָשִׁ֑ים לְמַטֵּ֣ה יְהוּדָ֔ה כָּלֵ֖ב בֶּן־יְפֻנֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And these [are the] names of the men: of [the] tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;

en.L: And these [are] the names of the men: for the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh,
en.B: These are the names of the men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh,
en.R: Here are their names: From the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh.

decisions.choice: Caleb son of Jephunneh: the faithful scout
decisions.reason: Caleb was Judah's scout, who urged the people to go up and take the land (13:6, 30; 14:6-9). He and Joshua were the only men of their generation spared to enter it (14:24, 30, 38; 26:65). He now helps to divide the land he had trusted the LORD to give.

decisions.choice: the order of the tribes: roughly from south to north
decisions.reason: The list in verses 19-28 runs in pairs, mostly in the order of the tribes' later land from south to north: Judah and Simeon, Benjamin and Dan, then Manasseh and Ephraim, Zebulun and Issachar, Asher and Naphtali (Joshua 15-19).

decisions.choice: a comma at the end
decisions.reason: Verses 19-28 are one list in Hebrew. Literal and Balanced end each name with a comma and close the list at verse 28; Readable gives each name its own sentence.

source.text: וּלְמַטֵּה֙ בְּנֵ֣י שִׁמְע֔וֹן שְׁמוּאֵ֖ל בֶּן־עַמִּיהֽוּד׃

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud;

en.L: and for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud,
en.B: from the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud,
en.R: From the tribe of Simeon, Shemuel son of Ammihud.

decisions.choice: Shemuel: a name that means "name of God" or "heard by God"
decisions.reason: Shemuel is the same name as Samuel. This Shemuel is not mentioned anywhere else.

decisions.choice: the tribe of Simeon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "the tribe of the sons of Simeon" here and for most of the tribes that follow. Balanced and Readable say "the tribe of Simeon", which means the same, in this verse and in verses 22-28. Literal keeps the full form.

source.text: לְמַטֵּ֣ה בִנְיָמִ֔ן אֱלִידָ֖ד בֶּן־כִּסְלֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon;

en.L: for the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon,
en.B: from the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon,
en.R: From the tribe of Benjamin, Elidad son of Chislon.

decisions.choice: of the tribe of Benjamin: the shorter form, as for Judah
decisions.reason: Like Judah in verse 19, Benjamin is named without "the sons of" and without "and". The variation in the list does not change the sense.

source.text: וּלְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵי־דָ֖ן נָשִׂ֑יא בֻּקִּ֖י בֶּן־יָגְלִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Dan, a leader, Bukki son of Jogli;

en.L: and for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Dan, a leader, Bukki son of Jogli,
en.B: from the tribe of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli,
en.R: From the tribe of Dan, the leader Bukki son of Jogli.

decisions.choice: a leader: the title given to each man from here on
decisions.reason: From this verse on each name is called "a leader", the title used in verse 18. The men in verses 19-21 hold it too, though the word is not repeated for them.

decisions.choice: the leader
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "the leader", which reads more naturally in a list than "a leader". As in verse 20, they say "the tribe of Dan" for "the tribe of the sons of Dan".

source.text: לִבְנֵ֣י יוֹסֵ֔ף לְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־מְנַשֶּׁ֖ה נָשִׂ֑יא חַנִּיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־אֵפֹֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: Of [the] sons of Joseph: of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Manasseh, a leader, Hanniel son of Ephod;

en.L: for the {{gender:children|sons}} of Joseph, for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Manasseh, a leader, Hanniel son of Ephod,
en.B: from the descendants of Joseph: from the tribe of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod,
en.R: From the descendants of Joseph: From the tribe of Manasseh, the leader Hanniel son of Ephod.

decisions.choice: the sons of Joseph: the two tribes descended from Joseph
decisions.reason: Jacob took Joseph's two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim, as his own, so that each became a tribe (Genesis 48:5). The heading "the sons of Joseph" covers both this verse and the next. The Manasseh meant here is the half of the tribe that settles west of the Jordan (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Ephod: a personal name
decisions.reason: Hanniel's father has the same name as the priest's garment, the ephod (Exodus 28:6), but here it is simply a man's name.

decisions.choice: descendants
decisions.reason: "Sons" here means the whole line descended from Joseph; Balanced and Readable say "descendants", which already includes everyone, so no setting is needed.

source.text: וּלְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־אֶפְרַ֖יִם נָשִׂ֑יא קְמוּאֵ֖ל בֶּן־שִׁפְטָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Ephraim, a leader, Kemuel son of Shiphtan;

en.L: and for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Ephraim, a leader, Kemuel son of Shiphtan,
en.B: from the tribe of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan,
en.R: From the tribe of Ephraim, the leader Kemuel son of Shiphtan.

decisions.choice: Ephraim after Manasseh: the second of Joseph's tribes
decisions.reason: Ephraim is the younger son, but he was given the first place in Jacob's blessing (Genesis 48:14-20). Here, as in 26:28-37, Manasseh comes first; the order in the list is not a ranking.

source.text: וּלְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־זְבוּלֻ֖ן נָשִׂ֑יא אֱלִיצָפָ֖ן בֶּן־פַּרְנָֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Zebulun, a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach;

en.L: and for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Zebulun, a leader, Elizaphan son of Parnach,
en.B: from the tribe of Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach,
en.R: From the tribe of Zebulun, the leader Elizaphan son of Parnach.

decisions.choice: Elizaphan: "my God has protected"
decisions.reason: The name means "my God has hidden" or "protected". A Levite of the same name appears in 3:30, but this is a different man, from the tribe of Zebulun.

source.text: וּלְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־יִשָׂשכָ֖ר נָשִׂ֑יא פַּלְטִיאֵ֖ל בֶּן־עַזָּֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Issachar, a leader, Paltiel son of Azzan;

en.L: and for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Issachar, a leader, Paltiel son of Azzan,
en.B: from the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan,
en.R: From the tribe of Issachar, the leader Paltiel son of Azzan.

decisions.choice: Paltiel: "God is my deliverance"
decisions.reason: The name means "God is my escape" or "deliverance". The same name is borne by another man in 2 Samuel 3:15.

source.text: וּלְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵי־אָשֵׁ֖ר נָשִׂ֑יא אֲחִיה֖וּד בֶּן־שְׁלֹמִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Asher, a leader, Ahihud son of Shelomi;

en.L: and for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Asher, a leader, Ahihud son of Shelomi,
en.B: from the tribe of Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi,
en.R: From the tribe of Asher, the leader Ahihud son of Shelomi.

decisions.choice: Asher: one of the northern tribes
decisions.reason: The last two pairs, Asher and Naphtali, settle in the far north of the land, along the coast and in the hills of Galilee (Joshua 19:24-39).

source.text: וּלְמַטֵּ֥ה בְנֵֽי־נַפְתָּלִ֖י נָשִׂ֑יא פְּדַהְאֵ֖ל בֶּן־עַמִּיהֽוּד׃

records.literal_gloss: And of [the] tribe of [the] sons of Naphtali, a leader, Pedahel son of Ammihud.

en.L: and for the tribe of the {{gender:children|sons}} of Naphtali, a leader, Pedahel son of Ammihud."
en.B: and from the tribe of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud."
en.R: From the tribe of Naphtali, the leader Pedahel son of Ammihud."

decisions.choice: Ammihud: a different man from the father of Shemuel
decisions.reason: Shemuel of Simeon (verse 20) is also "son of Ammihud", a common name; the two fathers belong to different tribes and are different men.

decisions.choice: the end of the list and of the LORD's words
alternatives: the speech runs on through verse 29
decisions.reason: The list closes with Naphtali, the tenth tribe. The LORD's speech, begun in verse 17, ends here; verse 29 is a closing summary.

source.text: אֵ֕לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה לְנַחֵ֥ל אֶת־בְּנֵֽי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בְּאֶ֥רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃פ

records.literal_gloss: These [are those] whom commanded Yahweh to apportion [to the] sons of Israel in [the] land of Canaan.

en.L: These [are those] whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded to give the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel their inheritance in the land of Canaan.
en.B: These are the men whom {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} commanded to divide the inheritance among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} in the land of Canaan.
en.R: These are the men {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the task of dividing the land of Canaan among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}.

decisions.choice: a closing summary in the narrator's voice
alternatives: the last words of the LORD's speech
decisions.reason: The verse speaks of the LORD in the third person and sums up verses 17-28. It is best read as the narrator's closing line, like 36:13, though the LORD sometimes speaks of himself by name and it could end his speech.

decisions.choice: to apportion: to put the people in possession of their inheritance
decisions.reason: The verb here means to give someone a share as their inheritance. The men named are to see that every tribe, clan and family receives its portion of Canaan, as is done in Joshua 14-19.

decisions.choice: gave the task of dividing
decisions.reason: Readable puts "commanded to apportion" as giving the men a task, which is what the command did.
